anchor.statement: Proposition B.2. With the axis data of Section B.1, there are Λ 0 and, for each Λ ≥ Λ 0 , an amplitude threshold C 0 ( Λ ) such that every C ≥ C 0 ( Λ ) admits an analytic axis profile with vanishing leading residual stress on 0 ≤ Y = Λ X ≤ 4.1. It has the form ϕ = ϕ∗ Φ , U = U ∗ + Λ−1 u, Π = Π 0 + Λ−1 I(g 2Φ2 ), g = ϕ∗ /C, (B.12)

correspondence.note: The existence theorem gives Λ0, then for each Λ ≥ Λ0 a threshold for C, and a profile analytic on one open set containing [0, 4.1] × [−1, 1] for all such Λ, C; the two structures carry the equations with vanishing leading residual stress, Φ(0, η) = 1, u(0, η) = 0, and (B.13) as a bound jetBound·K/(2Λ) on every mixed derivative for |Y| ≤ R < 20. The axis data δ∗, σ∗ are constructed inside the theorem from an admissible pressure datum.

links.doc:
The literal common-neighborhood assertion for the printed natural-axis
construction. All input data, the cutoff and the nonlinear coefficient
solution are constructed. The same open scaled rectangle works for every
sufficiently large scale and every allowed amplitude normalization.
